notes: Indianapolis, Marion County, IN. Operational Dec 1988. 2,175 t/day peak; ~6.5 MWe electric (modest); steam sold. One of the smaller Reworld plants. Illinois Basin CO2 storage (Mt. Simon Sandstone) in proximity — same formation as ADM Decatur. Low retrofit score due to small absolute CO2 volume and aging facility.

name: Drax Morehouse BioEnergy (Louisiana Biomass)
capacity_note: ~450 kt/yr wood pellets + biomass-fired generation (combined pellet manufacturing + power); Bastrop, Louisiana
operator: Drax Group plc (via Drax Biomass Inc.)
source: Drax Group annual report 2023; Drax Biomass Louisiana operations; GEM Wiki Drax Morehouse
notes: Bastrop, Morehouse Parish, LA. One of Drax's largest US pellet production facilities. Pellet drying and manufacturing releases biogenic CO2 (from wood drying steam boilers). Like Georgia Biomass (Waycross GA), the major biogenic CO2 release is at Drax UK where pellets are burned. Louisiana Gulf Coast location = excellent CO2 storage geography but the on-site CO2 source from drying is modest. Low retrofit score — the key BECCS opportunity for Drax biomass is at the UK combustion end, not these US manufacturing plants.

name: Evero Ince Bio Power (InBECCS)
capacity_note: 21.5 MWe waste-wood biomass; 170,000 t/yr waste wood
source: Evero Energy press releases 2024-2025; Bioenergy Insight Magazine; UK HyNet Track 1 deliverability assessment Oct 2024
notes: ACTIVE BECCS PROJECT. UK government-approved for HyNet Track 1 CCS retrofit. InBECCS project: 250,000 t CO2/yr capture planned, target operational 2030. CCS via HyNet North West pipeline to Liverpool Bay storage. One of UK's first commercial-scale BECCS plants. [CO2 basis: 170 kt/yr waste wood x ~1.4 tCO2/t; matches announced 250 kt/yr capture.]

name: Evero Mersey Bio Energy (BECCS)
capacity_note: 20.9 MWe waste-wood biomass; ~150,000 t/yr waste wood
source: Evero Energy press releases 2024; Energy Voice report Oct 2024; Chester Standard report
notes: HyNet Track 1 expansion candidate alongside Ince. Located near Widnes, Cheshire. Both Mersey and Ince plants together process >300,000 t/yr waste wood. CCS retrofit under development through HyNet. [CO2 basis: 150 kt/yr waste wood x ~1.4 tCO2/t; matches announced 200 kt/yr capture.]

name: Kent Renewable Energy (Sandwich CHP)
capacity_note: 28.1 MWe / 25 MWth biomass CHP; ~210 GWh/yr
source: Kent Renewable Energy Ltd website; Greenvolt acquisition announcement 2024; Bioenergy International; power-technology.com profile
notes: Biomass CHP burning wood chips and agricultural biomass. ~210.8 GWh generated in 2023. Saves ~45,000 t CO2/yr on fossil displacement basis. Located in Pfizer industrial area, Sandwich, Kent. Greenvolt acquisition completed ~Oct 2024.

name: Margam Green Energy (Port Talbot)
capacity_note: 40 MWe waste-wood biomass; 250,000 t/yr waste wood
source: Margam Green Energy website; Generandi/Greencoat acquisition report; Babcock & Wilcox Vølund case study
notes: £160M waste-wood-fired power station; operational since 2019. Processes contaminated waste wood including C&D waste without pre-treatment. Powers ~75,000 homes. O&M by Babcock & Wilcox Vølund. Adjacent to Port Talbot Steelworks site — decarbonisation cluster potential. [CO2 basis: 250 kt/yr waste wood x ~1.4 tCO2/t.]

name: Sleaford Renewable Energy Plant
capacity_note: 38.5 MWe straw-fired biomass; ~240,000 t/yr straw
source: Global Energy Monitor Sleaford REP entry; power-technology.com profile; BWSC reference page; electricityproduction.uk
notes: Agricultural straw-fired power station. Commissioned September 2014. Located at Eslaford Park, North Kesteven, Lincolnshire. BWSC operates under 15-yr agreement. Straw sourced within 50-mile radius. [CO2 basis: 240 kt/yr straw x ~1.35 tCO2/t.]

name: Snetterton Renewable Energy Plant
capacity_note: 44.2 MWe straw/biomass; ~300,000 t straw per year
source: power-technology.com Snetterton profile; PensionDanmark press release; IPP Journal project record
notes: 44.9 MWe straw-fired biomass plant in Breckland District, Norfolk. Commissioned April 2017. BWSC owner/operator. Saves ~300,000 t CO2 fossil displacement. Part of same UK straw-to-power cluster as Sleaford and Brigg.

name: Brigg Renewable Energy Plant
capacity_note: 40 MWe straw-fired biomass; 240,000 t/yr wheat straw
operator: BWSC North Lincs Ltd (JV: BWSC / PensionDanmark / CIP)
source: power-technology.com Brigg Biomass profile; BWSC reference; Renewables Now news 2016; New Civil Engineer
notes: Straw-fired 40 MWe power station at Glanford Vale Business Park, Scawby Brook, near Brigg, North Lincolnshire. Built on former British Sugar factory site. Commissioned early 2016. 240,000 t/yr wheat straw from within 50-mile radius. 15-yr BWSC O&M contract. [CO2 basis: 240 kt/yr wheat straw x ~1.35 tCO2/t.]

name: Wilton 10 (Sembcorp Teesside Biomass)
capacity_note: 30 MWe / 10 MWth biomass CHP; 300,000 t/yr wood waste
source: Wikipedia: Wilton power stations; power-technology.com Wilton 10 profile; Sembcorp press release 2007
notes: UK's first large-scale commercial wood-to-energy plant (opened Nov 2007). Burns 300,000 t/yr sustainable wood, sawmill waste and wood offcuts. Located within Wilton petrochemical complex — industrial CCS cluster opportunity (HyNet or Teesside cluster). Steam output piped to wider Wilton complex. [CO2 basis: 300 kt/yr wood waste x ~1.35 tCO2/t.]

name: SELCHP (South East London CHP)
capacity_note: 35 MWe EfW; 460,000 t/yr waste
source: Wikipedia: SELCHP; Veolia UK press release (25 years, 2019); SELCHP.com; Southwark Council website
notes: Opened November 1994; one of London's longest-operating EfW plants. Processes 460,000 t/yr; 35 MWe steam turbine. Located at Spa Road, Bermondsey/Deptford. Provides district heating. Biogenic fraction of MSW ~50% (EU average, Eurostat); ~0.21 Mt biogenic CO2/yr estimated (calc: 460,000 t × 0.5 biogenic × 0.9 combustion efficiency × ~1 tCO2/t biogenic waste).

name: Cory Riverside 1 (Belvedere EfW)
capacity_note: 66 MWe EfW; 750,000 t/yr waste
source: Cory Group website; power-technology.com Riverside RRF project; WSP case study; Cory sustainability emissions page
notes: One of Europe's largest single-site EfW plants. 750,000 t/yr capacity; 66 MWe. Cory Decarbonisation Project targets 1.4 Mt CO2 savings/yr from Riverside 1+2 by 2030 via CCS. Adjacent Riverside 2 (650,000 t, 61 MWe) under construction 2026. CCS pathway through Thames Estuary or East Coast cluster.

name: Lakeside EfW (Colnbrook)
capacity_note: 37 MWe EfW; 450,000 t/yr waste
source: Wikipedia: Lakeside EfW; Viridor website; Global Energy Monitor Lakeside EfW entry; Wikiwaste Lakeside EfW
notes: JV between Grundon Waste Management and Viridor. Located in Colnbrook, Slough near Heathrow. 450,000 t/yr permitted; 37 MWe. Biogenic CO2 estimated at 50% of combustion CO2 (EU MSW biogenic fraction).

name: Viridor Runcorn EfW
capacity_note: ~100 MWe total EfW (Phase 1+2); 1,100,000 t/yr waste
source: Viridor Runcorn EfW website; Letsrecycle.com capacity extension news; Keppel Seghers Phase 1 commissioning release; Global Energy Monitor Runcorn EfW entry; Viridor CCS project page
notes: UK's largest single-site EfW facility by waste throughput. 1.1 Mt/yr; Phase 1: 425,000 t, 35 MWe + 51 MWth steam. Powers ~211,000 homes equivalent. Viridor actively developing CCS retrofit — Runcorn CCS Project on company website. HyNet North West cluster proximity makes this a high-priority CCS candidate.

name: Severnside Energy Recovery Centre (Avonmouth)
capacity_note: 37 MWe EfW; 400,000 t/yr waste
source: Wikiwaste Severnside ERC; SUEZ UK blog; Global Energy Monitor Avonmouth ERF; PRIVA case study
notes: Waste primarily delivered by rail from West London and Bristol areas. Located adjacent to Seabank Power Station, Avonmouth industrial area. 400,000 t/yr; 37 MWe. Potential future CCS linkage to Portbury/Avonmouth CO2 logistics.

name: Beddington EfW (Sutton, South London)
capacity_note: 26 MWe EfW; 382,000 t/yr waste
source: Viridor Beddington ERF website; Wikiwaste Beddington EfW; Letsrecycle.com EA permit expansion
notes: Serves South London Waste Partnership (Croydon, Kingston, Merton, Richmond, Sutton). 25-yr PPP contract signed Nov 2014. 2 lines, Martin Reverse Acting Grate. Operational Jan 2020. Capacity increased to 382,286 t/yr under EA permit variation.

name: Ferrybridge Multifuel 1 (FM1)
capacity_note: 68 MWe multifuel EfW; ~700,000 t/yr
source: Wikiwaste FM1; Global Energy Monitor Ferrybridge Multifuel 1; power-technology.com FM1 project; enfinium company website
notes: 68 MWe, commissioned 2015. Located on site of former Ferrybridge C coal power station, Knottingley, West Yorkshire. Adjacent to FM2. Combined FM1+FM2 capacity 1.35 Mt/yr — largest residual waste EfW site in UK. Former coal infrastructure and grid connection aids CCS viability.

name: Javelin Park EfW (Gloucestershire)
capacity_note: 17.4 MWe gross / 14.5 MWe net EfW; 190,000 t/yr waste
source: Wikipedia: Gloucestershire EfW; Wikiwaste Javelin Park EfW; Gloucestershire County Council; FCC Environment UK website
notes: 25-yr contract with Gloucestershire County Council (awarded Dec 2011). Fully operational January 2020. 190,000 t/yr; 17.4 MWe gross. FCC Servicios Medio Ambiente acquired Urbaser's UK affiliate June 2024 — now FCC Environment UK. Smaller plant, lower CCS priority.

name: Newhurst Energy Recovery Facility (Shepshed)
capacity_note: 42 MWe EfW; 350,000 t/yr waste
source: Encyclis press release full operations; Global Energy Monitor Newhurst ERF; Newhursterf.co.uk; HZI reference Newhurst; Biffa press release Jan 2022
notes: 42 MWe, 350,000 t/yr. Located near Shepshed, Leicestershire. Full operations commenced 2025 after 3-yr construction/commissioning. Operated by Encyclis. Kanadevia Inova (HZI) technology. UK East Midlands location — potential Humber CCS cluster linkage.

name: Protos Energy Recovery Facility (Cheshire)
capacity_note: 49.9 MWe EfW; 400,000 t/yr waste
source: Protos ERF website; Green Investment Group Financial Close press release 2020; Kanadevia Inova press release; Global Energy Monitor Protos EfW
notes: 49.9 MWe; 400,000 t/yr; within Protos strategic energy hub near Ellesmere Port. Commissioning phase 2024-2025. Encyclis acquired plant 2025. Kanadevia Inova green-lit to build UK's first full-scale carbon capture facility at Protos — making this a HIGH-priority BECCS site. HyNet proximity for CO2 transport.

name: Rookery South ERF (Stewartby, Bedfordshire)
capacity_note: 60+ MWe EfW; 545,000 t/yr waste
source: Covanta/Reworldwaste press release Jan 2022; Kanadevia Inova handover release; Global Energy Monitor Rookery South; Central Bedfordshire Council
notes: 60+ MWe; 545,000 t/yr. Located in former brickworks at Stewartby, Bedfordshire. Operational since January 2022. JV: Covanta/EQT 80%, Veolia 20%.

name: Earls Gate Energy Centre (Grangemouth, Scotland)
capacity_note: 22 MWe / 33 MWth EfW; 216,000 t/yr waste
source: EUWID Recycling; Earls Gate Energy Centre website; Green Investment Group 2018 announcement; Brockwell Energy project page
notes: 216,000 t/yr; 22 MWe. Fully operational June 2024 after delays. Scotland's first major EfW plant. Located in Grangemouth petrochemical/industrial cluster — potential Acorn CCS pathway (Caledonian Clean Energy project / St Fergus). Co-owned Encyclis/Brockwell; HZI operates.

name: Sysav Malmö Waste-to-Energy Plant
capacity_note: ~100 MWth district heat; 600,000 t/yr waste
source: Wikipedia: SYSAV waste-to-energy plant; NIB financing article; Waste Today; Friotherm case study (heat pump); Nordic Investment Bank
notes: Treats ~600,000 t/yr waste from southern Skåne province. Covers ~60% of Malmö district heating. Also known as Sjölunda facility. 2019 total waste received: 887,100 t; 1,464,700 MWh heat + 189,500 MWh electricity. Sweden has active CCS policy for WtE (LULUCF framework); Sysav is a leading candidate.

name: Renova Sävenäs WtE (Göteborg)
capacity_note: 42 MWe / ~400 MWth district heat; ~70 t/hr waste
source: Global Energy Monitor Sävenäs WtE; Renova facilities page; Smart City Sweden Renova profile; CTC-N Renova efficient waste recovery
notes: Annual production: 1,506 GWh district heat + 279 GWh electricity (2018). ~70 t/hr waste throughput. 60% of electricity labelled biofuel origin. Provides ~1/3 of Göteborg heat demand. Active CCS interest in Swedish WtE sector; Göteborg location near port infrastructure for CO2 shipping.

name: Filbornaverket WtE (Helsingborg)
capacity_note: 18 MWe / 72 MWth EfW CHP; 220,000 t/yr waste
source: Smart City Sweden Filborna CHP profile; CTC-N Filborna; Bioenergy International: Öresundskraft SEK 228M CCS grant; power-technology.com Helsingborg WtE profile
notes: 72 MWth / 18 MWe, 220,000 t/yr. Commissioned 2013. Supplies ~60% of Helsingborg district heating baseload. Öresundskraft secured SEK 228M Swedish Energy Agency grant for Filbornaverket CCS project — ACTIVE CCS development. Biogenic CO2 capture target ~100,000 t/yr.

name: Högdalen WtE (Stockholm)
capacity_note: ~200 MWth district heat; 700,000 t/yr waste capacity
source: Smart City Sweden: Waste incineration at Högdalenverket; Waste incineration in Nordic countries (Norden 2024); Stockholm Exergi corporate reports
notes: Stockholm Exergi also operates KVV8 (already in database). Högdalen is a separate WtE facility receiving ~700,000 t/yr capacity; multiple lines. Major biogenic CO2 source co-located with Stockholm Exergi's BECCS programme — strong CCS synergy.

name: Tammervoima WtE (Tampere, Finland)
capacity_note: 58.5 MWth / ~20 MWe EfW; 160,000 t/yr MSW
source: Tammervoima plant website; HZI Steinmüller reference Tampere; Valmet automation case study; Tampere waste-to-energy PDF 2018
notes: Operational since January 2016. 160,000 t/yr MSW; 310 GWh heat + 90 GWh electricity annually. Address: Hyötyvoimankuja 1, 33680 Tampere. Covers 15% of Tampere heating/electricity consumption. Separate from Naistenlahti biomass CHP (different facility).

name: Helen Vuosaari Bioenergy Plant (Helsinki)
capacity_note: 260 MWth biomass heat-only; forest chips
source: Helen press releases 2018, 2022; Bioenergy International 2019; Global Energy Monitor Vuosaari power station; e-architect Helsinki profile
notes: 260 MW forest-chip biomass heating plant; produces ~25% of Helsinki district heat. Heat-only (no electricity currently, CHP conversion technically feasible per Helen). Reduces Helsinki CO2 by ~700,000 t/yr vs coal. Commissioned Dec 2022 (full production). Helen targets carbon neutrality by 2030. CO2 estimated: calc from 260 MWth × ~8,000 hrs × ~0.2 tCO2/MWh_biomass.

name: Statkraft Heimdal WtE (Trondheim)
capacity_note: 40 MWth WtE; ~220,000 t/yr MSW
source: Industry About Trondheim Heimdal; Aker Carbon Capture pre-FEED press release; SLB Capturi; IEA Bioenergy full-scale WtE CCS in Norway (2025)
notes: Provides >30% of Trondheim municipal heating demand. Aker Carbon Capture (now SLB Capturi) awarded pre-FEED for CO2 capture at 220,000 t CO2/yr. Active BECCS/WtE-CCS development. Norway has strong CCS policy and Northern Lights CO2 storage infrastructure.

name: Fynsværket (Odense, Denmark)
capacity_note: 35 MWe / 85 MWth biomass CHP (Unit 8 straw); overall site ~421 MW
source: Wikipedia: Fyn Power Station; Global Energy Monitor Fyns power station; power-technology.com Fynsværket 8 profile; Bioenergy International Andritz EcoFluid 2021
notes: Fynsværket 8 (straw biomass): 35 MWe / 85 MWth. Straw from local farmers. Andritz EcoFluid biomass boiler (new Bio Blok 2 project). Remaining units converted to biomass/waste. Odense is Denmark's 3rd largest city. CO2 estimate covers straw-fired unit; total site biogenic CO2 larger.

name: Studstrupværket (Aarhus, Denmark)
capacity_note: 700 MWe biomass CHP (converted from coal 2016)
source: Wikipedia: Studstrup Power Station; Biomass Magazine 2016; State of Green; Canadian Biomass Magazine; Global Energy Monitor Studstrup
notes: One of the world's largest biomass CHP plants — 700 MWe converted from coal to wood pellets Oct 2016. District heating for ~106,000 homes; electricity for ~230,000 homes. Annual wood pellet consumption ~1.6 Mt. Saves ~310,000 t fossil CO2/yr. High-value BECCS target — biogenic CO2 ~1.8 Mt/yr estimated. Note: Ørsted Avedøre already in database, this is Studstrup separately.

name: Borregaard Sarpsborg (Biorefinery / Sulphite Pulp)
capacity_note: ~168,000 t/yr specialty cellulose; 1M solid m³/yr wood input; bioethanol + lignin + vanillin
source: Borregaard Wikipedia; ETIP Bioenergy factsheet Borregaard; Borregaard CDP 2023 climate change submission; Borregaard annual report 2023
notes: World's most advanced biorefinery — sulphite process (not kraft). Produces specialty cellulose, lignin biopolymers, bioethanol (20M L/yr), vanillin. EU ETS covered. Uses 94% of wood feedstock. High-concentration CO2 in recovery boiler flue gas. Norway's Northern Lights storage proximity makes CCS attractive. Not a standard kraft mill — distinct chemical signature.

name: Billerud Gruvön Mill (Grums, Sweden)
capacity_note: ~550,000 t/yr packaging board + market pulp; KM7 machine 550,000 t/yr
source: Billerud Gruvön mill page; Google Maps coordinates 59.3401, 13.1149; packaging-gateway.com Gruvön expansion; Billerud Annual & Sustainability Report 2022; ANDRITZ flue gas treatment 2023
notes: One of Europe's leading fluting/liner/liquid packaging board mills. ~30 km west of Karlstad, Värmland. New soda recovery boiler expanded capacity. Black liquor recovery boiler is dominant CO2 source (~75% of mill CO2). Billerud has active decarbonisation programme. New ANDRITZ flue gas precipitator for recovery boiler. CO2 estimated: calc from 550,000 t pulp × ~1.0 t biogenic CO2/t pulp (Frontiers 2026 European average).

name: Billerud Skärblacka Mill (Norrköping)
capacity_note: ~460,000 t/yr kraft paper (MG kraft, sack paper, fluting)
source: Billerud Skärblacka mill page; Wikipedia: Billerud; euwid-paper.com PM10 startup; Billerud production units overview
notes: Specialises in white MG/MF kraft paper, brown sack paper, fluting. 460,000 t/yr. Located just outside Norrköping, Östergötland. PM10 paper machine started. Two laboratories for food and medical packaging R&D. CO2 estimate: calc from 460,000 t × ~1.0 tCO2/t.

name: Billerud Frövi/Rockhammar Mill
capacity_note: ~500,000 t/yr cartonboard + liquid packaging board
source: Billerud Frövi/Rockhammar mill page; Billerud Wikipedia; euwid-paper.com Frövi SP4 recovery boiler 2023 (SEK 2.6B investment)
notes: ~30 km north of Örebro, Västmanland. Produces cartonboard for luxury/consumer goods and liquid packaging. New SP4 recovery boiler inaugurated Sep 2023 (SEK 2.6B). Expanded pulp capacity enables higher CO2 capture potential. CO2 estimated: calc 500,000 t × ~1.0 tCO2/t.

name: SCA Obbola Mill (Umeå)
capacity_note: 725,000 t/yr kraftliner; world's largest kraftliner machine
source: SCA Obbola mill page; PULPAPERnews: world's largest kraftliner machine 2023; AFRY project page; Valmet lime kiln reference SCA Obbola
notes: Integrated kraftliner mill just outside Umeå, Västerbotten. New world's largest kraftliner machine commissioned 2023. 100% fossil-free lime kiln (Valmet). Baltic Sea deep-water harbour. ~725,000 t/yr production — generates very large biogenic CO2 stream from recovery boiler. High CCS retrofit attractiveness.

name: SCA Munksund Mill (Piteå)
capacity_note: 410,000 t/yr kraft paper (white + brown packaging paper)
source: SCA Munksund page; SCA Munksund expansion packaging-gateway.com; Valmet fossil-free lime kiln reference SCA Munksund
notes: 410,000 t/yr white/brown kraft packaging paper. Located in Piteå, Norrbotten. Adjacent to Smurfit Kappa Piteå — potential shared CCS infrastructure in Piteå port area. Valmet delivered fossil-free lime kiln. Uses spruce/pine from sustainably managed forests in Northern Sweden.

name: Smurfit Westrock Piteå (Kraftliner Mill)
capacity_note: 700,000 t/yr kraftliner (Europe's largest); sulphate mill with 3 pulp lines + 2 PMs
source: Smurfit Kappa Piteå mill page; Wikidata Q47156448 coordinates 65°18'55.8N 21°26'40E; Wagenborg case study; Valmet rebuild 2019; packaging-gateway.com upgrades
notes: Europe's largest kraftliner producer; 700,000 t/yr. Mill at Kolugnsvägen 30, 941 86 Piteå. Two softwood pulp lines, one hardwood line with bleach plant, recycled fibre line, two PMs. 90% exported. Active sustainability drive (combustion/cooking upgrades). Piteå port enables CO2 shipping. ~510 employees.

name: Holmen Braviken Paper Mill (Norrköping)
capacity_note: 605,000 t/yr newsprint/SC paper (mechanical pulp); 2 paper machines
source: Holmen Braviken mill page; Wikipedia: Braviken Paper Mill; Andritz rebuild completion June 2025; Valmet wash press 2023
notes: 605,000 t/yr printing/writing paper on Bråviken bay, outside Norrköping. 100% fresh wood fibre. Two PMs. Deepwater harbour. Mechanical pulp process (TMP) — lower biogenic CO2 per tonne than kraft mills (no recovery boiler), but large scale still significant. CO2 estimate is lower per tonne (~0.5 tCO2/t vs ~1.0 for kraft). Recently rebuilt PM for efficiency and flexibility (ANDRITZ June 2025).

name: Holmen Iggesund Mill (Iggesund, Sweden)
capacity_note: ~200,000 t/yr premium paperboard (Invercote); integrated chemical pulp mill
source: Holmen Iggesund mill page; iggesund.com about/locations; Wikipedia: Holmen Iggesund; euwid-paper.com cartonboard expansion 2023
notes: World-class kraft-based premium paperboard mill (Invercote) dating to 1685. Located on Hälsingland coast, Baltic Sea. ~200,000 t/yr premium board. Integrated bleached kraft pulp mill with recovery boiler. Holmen has active low-carbon agenda. Baltic Sea location enables CO2 ship transport.

name: UPM Kaukas Pulp Mill (Lappeenranta)
capacity_note: 700,000 t/yr bleached softwood kraft pulp (two lines)
source: UPM Pulp Kaukas page; UPM press release Kaukas investment; UPM global operations map entry; Wikimapia Kaukas paper mill
notes: On shore of Lake Saimaa, Lappeenranta, SE Finland. Integrated site: pulp mill + magazine paper mill + sawmill + UPM Lappeenranta biorefinery (HVO diesel). 700,000 t/yr two-line kraft mill. Recovery boiler generates dominant biogenic CO2 stream. UPM committed to carbon neutrality — CCS interest rising.

name: UPM Kymi Pulp Mill (Kouvola)
capacity_note: 870,000 t/yr bleached softwood + birch kraft pulp (expanded 2016)
source: UPM Pulp Kymi page; UPM press release Kymi expansion Jan 2016; GlobeNewswire Kymi opening; ANDRITZ pulp drying world record
notes: 870,000 t/yr (expanded 2016; €160M investment). Located in Kuusankoski, Kouvola along River Kymi, SE Finland. Integrated with paper mill. ANDRITZ pulp drying plant achieved world record throughput. One of the largest single-site kraft pulp mills in Europe — major biogenic CO2 point source. UPM temporarily curtailed production Aug 2024 (market conditions).

name: UPM Pietarsaari Pulp Mill (Jakobstad)
capacity_note: 800,000 t/yr bleached softwood + birch kraft pulp
source: UPM Pulp Pietarsaari page; UPM biochemicals global operations map (location 87); UPM ABB reference story
notes: Gulf of Bothnia, western Finland (Jakobstad/Pietarsaari). 800,000 t/yr — co-located with Alholma sawmill and Alholmens Kraft power plant (already in database). Integrated industrial cluster. Softwood and birch pulp. Recovery boiler generates large concentrated biogenic CO2 stream ideal for CCS.

name: Stora Enso Oulu Mill
capacity_note: 750,000 t/yr consumer board + kraftliner + softwood pulp (by 2027)
source: Stora Enso Oulu mill page; packaging-gateway.com Oulu new board line; Packaging Europe €1.1B investment article; Stora Enso press release Aug 2025 inauguration; ANDRITZ Stora Enso Oulu
notes: Deep-sea harbour at Oulu, northern Finland. €1.1B investment in consumer packaging board line (inaugurated Aug 2025). Target 750,000 t/yr by 2027 (folding boxboard + kraftliner + softwood pulp). 90% CO2 reduction claimed for new board line vs old coal process. Large recovery boiler remains dominant biogenic CO2 source.

name: Stora Enso Imatra Mills (Kaukopää + Tainionkoski)
capacity_note: ~1,000,000 t/yr consumer packaging board + pulp (combined two units)
source: Stora Enso Imatra mill page; Paper360 May 2019; Stora Enso Wikipedia; Wikimapia Stora Enso Imatra Paper Mill; coords ~61.249, 28.857 (Imatra city)
notes: Two integrated production units (Kaukopää + Tainionkoski) in Imatra, E Finland near Russian border. ~1 Mt/yr liquid packaging board and consumer packaging board. One of the world's largest LPB producers. 90%+ exported. Two recovery boilers — large concentrated biogenic CO2 point source.

name: Stora Enso Sunila Mill (Kotka)
capacity_note: 370,000 t/yr bleached softwood kraft pulp; lignin extraction biorefinery
source: Stora Enso Sunila mill investment press release 2013; IEA Bioenergy Sunila biorefinery; Stora Enso Wikipedia; bioenergy-news.com Sunila
notes: 370,000 t/yr bleached softwood kraft pulp. Located at Sunila, near Kotka, S Finland. €32M biorefinery investment to extract lignin from black liquor — replaces up to 90% of natural gas with lignin. Lignin extraction reduces recovery boiler load slightly but still major biogenic CO2 source.

name: Metsä Fibre Rauma Pulp Mill
capacity_note: 650,000 t/yr bleached softwood kraft pulp (Metsä Strong brand)
source: Metsä Fibre Rauma mill page; paperage.com Joutseno restart Dec 2025; metsagroup.com pulp production overview
notes: ECF bleached softwood pulp (Metsä Strong); 650,000 t/yr. Produces biochemicals and bioenergy alongside pulp. Rauma port enables CO2 ship export. One of four Metsä Fibre Finnish mills. Production temporarily curtailed 2025 (market conditions) but core asset.

name: Metsä Fibre Joutseno Pulp Mill
capacity_note: 690,000 t/yr bleached softwood kraft pulp
source: Metsä Fibre Joutseno mill page; paperage.com Joutseno restart Dec 2025; coordinates: Haukilahdentie 27, Joutseno ~61.118, 28.502
notes: 690,000 t/yr. Located in Joutseno (Lappeenranta municipality), SE Finland on Lake Saimaa shores, 20 km N of Lappeenranta. Restarted Dec 2025 after temporary shutdown. Co-located with Metsä Board BCTMP mill. Recovery boiler dominant biogenic CO2 source.

name: MVR Hamburg (Müllverwertung Rugenberger Damm)
capacity_note: 320,000 t/yr MSW; CHP (electricity + steam + district heat); Rugenberger Damm, Hamburg-Altenwerder port
operator: MVR Müllverwertung Rugenberger Damm GmbH & Co. KG (Stadtreinigung Hamburg / Remondis 49%)
source: Klean Industries MVR profile; Stadtreinigung Hamburg MVR page; ITAD plant register; calc: 320 kt × 0.56 t CO₂/t MSW × 0.50 biogenic fraction
notes: Operational since 1999. Steam sold to industrial customers; electricity and district heat to Neuwiedenthal. No confirmed CCS. Hamburg WtE fleet totals ~5 plants; MVR is the dedicated MSW facility. Germany exploring CO₂ storage framework (KSpG reform 2024) — medium retrofit score.

name: MHKW Frankfurt am Main Nordweststadt
capacity_note: 525,600 t/yr MSW; ~28 MWe + 500,000 MWh/yr heat; Frankfurt Nordweststadt industrial zone
operator: MHKW Müllheizkraftwerk Frankfurt am Main GmbH (FES 50% + Mainova AG 50%)
source: GEM Wiki Frankfurt Waste-to-Energy power station; MHKW Frankfurt company profile (HRB 56310); FES Frankfurt subsidiaries page; calc: 525.6 kt × 0.55 t CO₂/t × 0.50 biogenic
notes: District owned by City of Frankfurt and Mainova. Generates ~200,000 MWh electricity and ~500,000 MWh heat. No CCS announced. Hydrogen blend trial for CO₂ reduction reported 2024 (partial fossil-CO₂ mitigation only). Frankfurt has stated no plans for WtE CCS as of 2026.

name: GML Gemeinschafts-Müllheizkraftwerk Ludwigshafen
capacity_note: 390,000 t/yr; 2 × 20 MWe (40 MWe total); Bürgermeister-Grünzweig-Str. 87, Ludwigshafen
operator: GML Gemeinschafts-Müllheizkraftwerk Ludwigshafen GmbH (MVV Umwelt stake)
source: MVV Energie TREA/GML profile; Steinmüller Babcock modernization announcement; CEWEP GML strategic comms; calc: 390 kt × 0.56 t CO₂/t × 0.50 biogenic
notes: Two modern incineration lines; modernized ~2018–2019 (Steinmüller Babcock). Process steam to BASF Chemiepark Ludwigshafen — large industrial steam customer adjacent to site. Strategic location near BASF could enable CO₂ utilization co-located with chemical synthesis.

name: AVA Augsburg (Abfallverwertungsanlage)
capacity_note: 350,000 t/yr residual + 90,000 t/yr biowaste; ~25 MWe; includes biowaste AD fermentation plant
operator: AVA Abfallverwertungsanlage Augsburg GmbH & Co. KG (ZAW public authority)
source: AVA Augsburg WtERT best practice case study; GEM Wiki AVA Augsburg power station; ZAW Augsburg public reports
notes: Integrated WtE plus biowaste anaerobic digestion — biogenic fraction higher than typical MSW-only plants due to organic waste fraction. ~90,000 t/yr biowaste separately fermented for biogas. Combined biogenic CO₂ is correspondingly higher. No CCS confirmed.

name: MVA Bonn Müllverwertungsanlage
capacity_note: ~180,000 t/yr MSW; steam exported to adjacent Stadtwerke Bonn CHP plant for electricity + district heat generation
operator: MVA Müllverwertungsanlage Bonn GmbH (Stadtwerke Bonn subsidiary)
source: Returo MVA Bonn facts & figures; Returo WtE plants page; Bloomberg MVA Bonn profile
notes: Steam-only model: MVA produces steam, adjacent SWB CHP converts to electricity (~97,000 MWh/yr) and district heat (~182,000 MWh/yr). Smaller throughput than other German WtE plants. No CCS plans.

name: TREA Leuna (Thermische Restabfallbehandlungs- und Energieverwertungsanlage)
capacity_note: 390,000 t/yr (2 × 195,000 t); 2 × 20 MWe; process steam to InfraLeuna/Chemiepark Leuna
operator: MVV Umwelt Asset GmbH (MVV Energie AG subsidiary)
source: MVV Energie TREA Leuna EfW plant page; Hitachi Zosen Inova TREA district heat press release; Envi-Con reference Leuna; calc: 390 kt × 0.56 × 0.50 biogenic
notes: Co-located with InfraLeuna Chemiepark — process steam sold to large industrial complex with numerous chemical manufacturers. Operational since 2005, expanded 2007. District heat extraction system added by Hitachi Zosen Inova. Chemiepark proximity is interesting for potential CO₂ utilization.

name: EEW Knapsack Hürth
capacity_note: 320,000 t/yr RDF/SRF; ~118,000 MWh/yr electricity; Knapsack Chemiepark near Cologne
operator: EEW Energy from Waste GmbH (Knapsack plant)
source: EEW Knapsack plant page; GEM Wiki Germany WtE register; calc: 320 kt × 0.56 × 0.50 biogenic
notes: RDF/SRF (Refuse Derived Fuel/Substitute Recovered Fuel) input — somewhat higher fossil fraction vs. household MSW. Located in Knapsack chemical park near Cologne/Hürth. Co-located industrial heat users. No CCS confirmed.

name: AVG Köln RMVA (Restmüllverbrennungsanlage)
capacity_note: ~900,000 t/yr (Germany's highest-throughput WtE); ~87 MWe; Cologne-Niehl port area
operator: AVG Abfallentsorgungs- und Verwertungsgesellschaft Köln mbH (Stadtwerke Köln)
source: AVG Köln website; GEM Wiki AVG Köln RMVA; Superlative Made in Germany AVG article; calc: 900 kt × 0.56 × 0.50 biogenic
notes: Germany's highest-throughput WtE plant by waste processed (~900 kt/yr). Rhine-side location with potential for CO₂ transport via river corridor or pipeline to North Sea storage. No CCS confirmed. NRW state exploring CCS framework — medium retrofit score.

name: MVA Pfaffenwald Stuttgart
capacity_note: ~38 MWe; large MSW throughput; Stuttgart-Münster industrial area
operator: Abfallverwertungsgesellschaft des Landkreises Ludwigsburg mbH (AVL) / AWG Stuttgart
source: GEM Wiki Pfaffenwald power station; CEWEP interactive map; RWTH Aachen WtE Germany status study 2020
notes: One of several Stuttgart-area WtE plants. Baden-Württemberg has several WtE facilities. No CCS plans. Germany has been slow to develop WtE CCS — regulatory uncertainty remains key barrier (KSpG revision still pending full implementation).

name: SYCTOM Ivry-Paris XIII (Centre de Traitement Ivry-Paris 13)
capacity_note: ~720,000 t/yr household waste (largest French WtE facility); steam to CPCU Paris district heating; two furnace-boiler units × 50 t/h
operator: SUEZ (operator since 2011); SYCTOM (Inter-municipal authority owner — 90 municipalities, 6.5 M inhabitants)
source: SUEZ Ivry-Paris XIII reference page; SYCTOM activity report; CEWEP WtE in Paris presentation; SolVair SYCTOM case study
notes: Partly in Paris 13th arrondissement, partly in Ivry-sur-Seine. Largest WtE in Île-de-France and among largest in France. Steam to CPCU (Paris district heating, >500 km pipes). Major renovation/rebuilding project ongoing as of 2020s — new plant planned for ~2030 at this site. New-build could integrate CCS from design.

name: SYCTOM Issy-les-Moulineaux (UVE Issy)
capacity_note: ~460,000 t/yr household waste; 3 furnace lines; suburb of Paris, Hauts-de-Seine
source: SYCTOM annual statistics; CEWEP France WtE data; calc: 460 kt × 0.56 × 0.50 biogenic
notes: Second major Paris-region SYCTOM plant. No CCS plans. France is building out CCS infrastructure (Dunkirk DUNCO₂ hub, Normandy corridor) but WtE has not been prioritized for near-term. Long-term rebuild plans may enable CCS-readiness.

name: Lagunes de Fos-sur-Mer UVE (Marseille region)
capacity_note: ~420,000 t/yr; Fos-sur-Mer industrial port zone near Marseille
operator: SEM (Société d'Économie Mixte) Énergie Environnement Provence; operated by Suez
source: CEWEP French WtE data; French Ministry of Ecology SINOE waste database; calc: 420 kt × 0.55 × 0.50 biogenic
notes: Located in Fos-sur-Mer (Port of Marseille industrial zone — Marseille-Fos port is among largest in Europe). Industrial cluster has active CCS investigation for cement/steel. Medium retrofit score due to potential integration with emerging Fos-sur-Mer industrial CO₂ cluster.

name: Indaver Doel / SLECO Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: 1,200,000 t/yr total site; SLECO fluidized-bed: 447,000 t/yr non-hazardous waste + sludge; 3 turbines ~85 MWe total
operator: Indaver NV (SLECO JV: Indaver + Veolia/SUEZ); Indaver holds majority in Doel complex
source: Indaver Doel CEWEP plant visit presentation; GEM Wiki SLECO Waste-to-Energy; Indaver Belgium activities page; Indaver annual data
notes: Doel site: largest integrated waste treatment complex in Belgium, handling 1.2 Mt/yr total. SLECO uses fluidized bed technology (3 units) for sludge + industrial waste — higher biogenic fraction than MSW grate. E-Wood plant (non-recyclable wood waste, 20 MWe) also on-site. Port of Antwerp-Bruges proximity offers CO₂ transport infrastructure access. Belgium has emerging CCS CO₂ hub plans in Antwerp port.

name: ISVAG Wilrijk Antwerp Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: 200,000 t/yr MSW; ~10.5 MWe; Wilrijk (Antwerp agglomeration)
operator: ISVAG (Intercommunale voor Slib en Vuilverwijdering Antwerpse Gemeenten)
source: ISVAG Dublix Technology reference; IndustryAbout Gent incineration data; ISVAG CEWEP case study; calc: 200 kt × 0.55 × 0.50 biogenic
notes: Inter-municipal plant serving 1+ million Antwerp residents. Smaller capacity than Indaver Doel. Antwerp port CO₂ cluster (ECLUSE initiative, Ineos/Fluxys CCS planning) could make CCS retrofit attractive in mid-2030s despite small scale.

name: IVAGO Gent Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: 100,000 t/yr MSW; 4.2 MWe; Proeftuinstraat 43, Gent
source: IndustryAbout Gent Incineration Plant; Dublix Technology IVAGO reference; GEM coordinates from Open Infrastructure Map area
notes: Small plant serving Gent area. At 4.2 MWe too small for economical standalone CCS. Potential for network aggregation with larger Flemish WtE plants. Low retrofit score due to small scale.

name: KEZO Hinwil Waste-to-Energy (Kehrichtverwertung Zürcher Oberland)
capacity_note: ~120,000 t/yr MSW; 12.5 MWe; Im Fennen 1a, 8867 Niederurnen (Glarus canton); planning new 2030 MSWI plant
source: KEZO CCS page (kva-linth.ch/energie-umwelt/ccs); Carbon Herald KEZO/Sulzer CO₂ capture pilot; CCUSNetwork KEZO entry; CATACARB HPC pilot press release 2025
notes: CCS PILOT ACTIVE (2025): Sulzer/CATACARB Hot Potassium Carbonate pilot capturing ~1,000 t CO₂/yr for use by adjacent greenhouse. Planning new 2030 MSWI plant — target 120,000 t/yr capture on new plant. Also co-hosts Climeworks first commercial DAC plant (separate facility on same site). High retrofit score as first Swiss WtE with active CCS pilot and new-build integration target.

name: KVA Hagenholz Zürich
capacity_note: ~430,000 t/yr MSW + sewer sludge; ~35 MWe; largest single-site biogenic CO₂ source in Zürich canton
operator: ERZ Entsorgung + Recycling Zürich (City of Zürich)
source: BAFU Swiss CCS & NETs report 2024; ETH DEMO UPCARMA WP4 scaling study; Swiss WtE sewer sludge incinerator pilot documentation
notes: CCS PILOT REPORTED: Hagenholz is the biggest single CO₂ point source in Zürich; city studying CCS. A sewer sludge co-incineration test bed for CO₂ capture technology piloted there is part of plans to equip the much larger Hagenholz main waste incinerator. Swiss BAFU/ETH study identifies Hagenholz as a priority site for CCUS chain scale-up. High retrofit score due to active planning and scale.

name: KVA Linth (Kehrichtverwertungsanlage Linthgebiet)
capacity_note: 120,000 t/yr MSW; 12.5 MWe; planning new 2030 MSWI facility; Niederurnen, Glarus
operator: Zweckverband Kehrichtverwertung Linthgebiet (KEZO and KVA Linth are two different Glarus/Zürich Oberland plants)
source: KVA Linth website; CCUS Network KVA Linth entry; Sulzer/KEZO pilot (different but adjacent plant); opendata.swiss KVA geodata
notes: Separate plant from KEZO Hinwil. KVA Linth also studying CCS integration for the planned 2030 new facility. Switzerland's CO₂ law and net-zero pathway explicitly include WtE CCS as a negative emission measure. High retrofit score for CCS readiness in new-build plan.

name: Wien Energie Spittelau Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: ~250,000 t/yr MSW; ~85 MWth thermal; 60,000 households district heating; Vienna 9th district (Hundertwasser building)
operator: Wien Energie GmbH (City of Vienna 100% owned)
source: Wien Energie Spittelau pages; GreenEnergyLab Spittelau heat project; Waste-to-Energy World article 50 years Hundertwasser incinerator
notes: Iconic Hundertwasser-designed building; Vienna landmark. Mainly district heating (60,000+ households). Small electrical output (~40,000 MWh/yr). Low retrofit score due to urban setting, small scale, and no announced CCS plans. Austria lacks CO₂ storage infrastructure; low national CCS policy priority.

name: Energie AG Wels Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: 300,000+ t/yr residual waste (2 lines); 100% district heat for Wels city (14,800 households)
operator: Energie AG Umwelt Service GmbH (Energie AG Oberösterreich subsidiary)
source: INP International Projects AVE Wels reference; Energie AG Umwelt Service district heat Wels report; Austrian WtE whitebook
notes: Upper Austria. Operational since 1991. Supplies 100% of Wels district heating. Two incineration lines. Austria has no CO₂ storage infrastructure — all WtE plants are low retrofit score. Some discussion of CO₂ use (greenhouses, food & beverage) but no geological storage pathway.

name: TERSA Sant Adrià de Besòs (Barcelona Waste-to-Energy)
capacity_note: 360,000 t/yr MSW (3 lines); ~200,000 MWh/yr electricity; Sant Adrià del Besòs, Barcelona metropolitan area
operator: TERSA (Tractament i Eliminació de Residus SA) — public company (AMB/Barcelona)
source: Grup Tersa waste-to-energy page; Lab.fr Barcelona WtE plant profile; SICK TERSA emission measurement case study; ResearchGate LCA 2022
notes: Barcelona Metropolitan Area public company. Inaugurated 1975, rebuilt 1997. Three treatment lines. No CCS plans. Spain has very limited CO₂ storage infrastructure; no policy framework for WtE CCS. Low retrofit score.

name: Zabalgarbi Bilbao Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: ~540,000 t/yr MSW + industrial waste; ~57 MWe (waste fraction, gas turbine add ~50 MWe); Basque Country
operator: Zabalgarbi S.A. (FCC Medio Ambiente + Diputación Foral de Vizcaya JV)
source: Zabalgarbi data-of-interest page; GEM Wiki Zabalgarbi power station; FCC Medio Ambiente WtE page; ScienceDirect exergy analysis case study
notes: Hybrid WtE + gas turbine plant (combined cycle). MSW fraction provides ~300,000–400,000 t/yr waste, supplemented by natural gas combined cycle for higher efficiency. Annual net: ~650 GWh. No CCS plans. Basque Country has CCS research but no active WtE CCS projects.

name: A2A Brescia Lamarmora Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: ~750,000 t/yr MSW (total Brescia WtE complex); ~85–117 MWe; one of the largest WtE complexes in Italy
operator: A2A S.p.A. (formerly ASM Brescia / AEM Brescia)
source: GEO Global Energy Observatory Brescia WtE (geoid/2429); A2A WtE plants page; ESG News A2A $120M sustainability investment; CEWEP A2A flue gas condensation
notes: Brescia WtE is a CHP complex (electricity + district heating for Bergamo, Brescia, Milan networks). A2A investing €120M for sustainability/efficiency upgrades. Italy developing CO₂ storage framework for offshore Adriatic storage (ENI CCS projects). A2A has expressed interest in net-zero but no WtE CCS announcement. Medium retrofit score.

name: A2A Silla 2 Milano Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: 550,000 t/yr MSW (3 lines); ~59 MWe; northwest Milan near Figino
source: GEM Wiki Silla 2 power station; Silla 2 municipality Milan page; Technital Silla 2 project profile; ValveIT Silla 2 project sheet
notes: Three identical combustion lines with mobile grate technology. CHP — electricity + Milan district heating. Municipality of Milan is a shareholder in A2A. No confirmed CCS plans. ENI Ravenna hub (offshore Adriatic) could eventually serve northern Italy WtE clusters.

name: Acea Ambiente San Vittore del Lazio Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: ~650,000 t/yr MSW (3 lines); ~49 MWe total (13.9 MWe line 1 + 17.5 MWe × 2 lines); Lazio's largest WtE
operator: Acea Ambiente S.r.l. (Acea Group; partial Roma Capitale ownership)
source: Acea Group San Vittore plant page; Acea Ambiente a-ambiente.it San Vittore plant; Acea annual sustainability reports 2022–2023
notes: Frosinone province (southeast of Rome). Largest WtE in Lazio. Three processing lines. Acea Group is Rome's public utility. No CCS plans. Central Italy has limited onshore CO₂ storage; offshore central/southern Italy storage potential is under early assessment (ENI).

name: Attero Moerdijk Waste-to-Energy (AEC Moerdijk)
capacity_note: 1,045,000 t/yr MSW (4 incineration lines); ~125 MWe; Moerdijk industrial port
operator: Attero B.V. (The Circular Company; previously AVR)
source: IndustryAbout Moerdijk Incineration Plant; GEM Wiki AEC Moerdijk; Power-Technology Moerdijk WtE profile; Attero locations page
notes: One of the largest WtE plants in Europe. CHP + large electricity export. Port of Moerdijk gives excellent CO₂ transport access to North Sea storage via Rotterdam CO₂ corridor (Porthos project). Attero publishes sustainability targets — exploring CCS pathways. High retrofit score: scale + port infrastructure + Netherlands CCS policy leadership.

name: HVC Alkmaar Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: ~1,200,000 t/yr MSW (~68–93 MWe); Boekelermeer polder, Alkmaar, North Holland
operator: HVC N.V. (100% public; 49 municipalities + 6 water boards in North Holland/Flevoland)
source: Power-Technology HVC Alkmaar WtE profile; GEM Wiki HVC Alkmaar; EIB project 20060306 (HVC Alkmaar Biomass); ABB Migrating Dutch WtE reference
notes: One of the largest WtE plants in the Netherlands by waste throughput. Also has co-located biomass CHP unit. Public ownership by 49 municipalities aligns with Dutch WtE CCS policy goals. Amsterdam-Alkmaar industrial corridor — potential CO₂ transport pipeline access. High retrofit score.

name: ARN B.V. Nijmegen Waste-to-Energy (Weurt)
capacity_note: ~410,000 t/yr MSW; 27 MWe + 800 TJ/yr heat (6,400 homes); Weurt, Gelderland
source: Power-Technology ARN Nijmegen WtE; TRIA International ARN profile; ARN B.V. IkNijmegen listing; Gelderland waste authority annual data
notes: Operational since 1987. Weurt (Beuningen municipality, near Nijmegen). Diaper recycling pioneering project. Netherlands CCS policy actively supports WtE CCS — ARN is a candidate for future Porthos network extension or regional CO₂ collection point.

name: KHK Kraków Eco-Incinerator (ZTPOK)
capacity_note: 220,000 t/yr MSW; 32 MWe + district heat; POSCO E&C constructed; operational 2016
source: EC Regional Policy Kraków WtE project; IntechOpen Kraków WtE case study; CEWEP Kraków plant control article; CCS4Krakow project page; POSCO E&C completion press release
notes: CCS4KRAKOW PROJECT: Active EU/Norway-funded feasibility study (CCS4Krakow.eu) exploring CO₂ capture, transport, and storage from this plant. Poland-Norway bilateral programme. First Polish WtE plant with active CCS investigation. Medium retrofit score due to early-stage feasibility rather than FID.

name: ITPOK Poznań Energy from Waste
capacity_note: 210,000 t/yr MSW; ~17.6 MWe + 34 MW district heat; operational 2016; Suez Zielona Energia operated
operator: Suez Zielona Energia sp. z o.o. (SUEZ; Marguerite fund infrastructure)
source: Suez Zielona Energia ITPOK page; Kanadevia-Inova Poznań reference; Power-Technology Poznan EfW; EIB Poznan EfW PPP case study
notes: Kanadevia (Hitachi Zosen) grate technology. 2 × 13.2 t/h lines, 63 MW thermal. PPP project with Marguerite infrastructure fund. Poland developing national CCS strategy but no WtE-specific framework. Operational efficiently — potential future network node.

name: ZTPOK Bydgoszcz Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: ~180,000 t/yr MSW; ~13 MWe; operational 2016; ProNatura operated
source: Power-Technology Bydgoszcz WtE profile; Termomeccanica WtE Bydgoszcz reference; MDPI Energy Efficiency Polish WtE analysis 2024
notes: Thermomeccanica grate technology. Medium capacity among Polish plants. Part of Kuyavia-Pomerania region. No CCS plans. Poland's WtE fleet is newer (all post-2013) but coal-heavy national energy system reduces policy urgency for WtE CCS.

name: Mercer Stendal Kraft Pulp Mill (Zellstoff Stendal)
capacity_note: 740,000 t/yr NBSK pulp; 148 MWe green electricity; Arneburg on Elbe River, Saxony-Anhalt
source: Mercer International Stendal operations page; GEM Wiki Stendal Mill power station; Mercer annual reports; calc: 740 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt × 1.0 (pulp and energy boiler combined)
notes: One of the largest single-line kraft pulp mills in Europe by capacity. 148 MWe biomass power plant — one of Germany's largest biomass electricity generators. Elbe River location. No CCS announced. Germany pulp mills (also Rosenthal) identified in academic BECCS potential studies as major biogenic CO₂ sources. Medium retrofit score.

name: Mercer Rosenthal Kraft Pulp Mill
capacity_note: 360,000 t/yr NBSK pulp; ~400,000 MWh/yr green electricity; Rosenthal am Rennsteig, Thuringia
source: Mercer Rosenthal operations page; AFRY climate-neutral pulp production study; Canadian Biomass Magazine Mercer emissions article; calc: 360 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt
notes: Thuringian Forest location. Mercer is extracting lignin from black liquor at pilot scale (1 t/day). AFRY study on path to climate-neutral pulp production cites Rosenthal as key German site. Lime kiln conversion from fossil fuels to renewable energy under study. No CCS confirmed at German mills.

name: Sappi Ehingen Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~160,000 t/yr dissolved sulphite pulp (HW+SW); integrated paper mill; Danube River, Baden-Württemberg
operator: Sappi Europe S.A. (Sappi Ltd, South Africa)
source: Sappi Ehingen Mill factsheet; Sappi Ehingen EMAS report 2024; Sappi ratcheting-up pulp integration article
notes: World's first chlorine-free bleaching plant. ~85% of primary energy from biogenic fuels (black liquor, biogas, bark). Danube River location. Sulphite pulp not kraft — smaller recovery boiler CO₂ stream than kraft mills. Sappi has sustainability program but no CCS announced. The mill is smaller than major kraft mills but has very high biogenic energy fraction.

name: Sappi Alfeld Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~127,750 t/yr dissolved sulphite pulp; integrated paper mill; Leine River, Lower Saxony
source: Sappi Alfeld Mill page; Sappi Alfeld restructure consultation 2024; pulp-paperworld.com PM2 rebuild article
notes: Near Hanover. Five digesters × 250 m³. ~350 t/day pulp. Sappi Alfeld is under restructuring review (consultation announced 2024) — potential capacity reduction or closure risk. Lower retrofit score due to business uncertainty and smaller scale. Sulphite process.

name: Fibre Excellence Tarascon Pulp Mill (Provence)
capacity_note: ~220,000 t/yr bleached kraft pulp (BHKP); Chemin des Radoubs, 13156 Tarascon, Bouches-du-Rhône
operator: Fibre Excellence Group (privately held; supported by Caisse des Dépôts)
source: Fibre Excellence Provence mill page; EIB EUR 40M loan to Navigator Figueira da Foz (separate, used as comp); EUWID Tarascon secured article; Fibre Excellence €190M decarbonization investment plan 2027 ('Choose France')
notes: South of France, on Rhône River. Fibre Excellence committed to €190M investment by 2027 (France national industrial investment program) for fluff pulp expansion and decarbonization. Rhône River corridor could facilitate CO₂ transport to Mediterranean offshore storage or Dunkirk/Normandy storage via future pipeline network.

name: Fibre Excellence Saint-Gaudens Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~280,000 t/yr kraft pulp; Haute-Garonne (Occitanie), south of France
source: Fibre Excellence Saint-Gaudens mill page; EUWID Saint-Gaudens articles (production interruptions 2021, resumption 2023); paper-world.com Fibre Excellence Saint-Gaudens
notes: Pyrénées foothills location. Resumed production 2023 after major maintenance/modernization stop. No CCS plans. Remote from French CO₂ transport infrastructure. Lower retrofit score than Tarascon due to inland location and intermittent operational history.

name: Mondi Frantschach Kraft Pulp & Sack Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~280,000 t/yr sack kraft paper + speciality market pulp; Frantschach-Sankt Gertraud, Carinthia
source: Mondi Group Frantschach location page; Mondi Frantschach €20M investment press release 2021; Andritz spectrum Frantschach recovery boiler start-up
notes: Carinthia valley location. Mondi Frantschach is one of the world's most advanced sack kraft paper mills. Energy self-sufficient for many years; exports heat to communities. Uses ~1.4M m³ pulpwood/yr. No CCS. Austria has no CO₂ storage sites. Low retrofit score.

name: Sappi Gratkorn Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~250,000 t/yr kraft pulp + 950,000 t/yr coated paper; River Mur, north of Graz, Styria
source: Sappi Gratkorn Mill page; Sappi co-creating coal-to-renewables shift at Gratkorn; Paper Age Gratkorn biomass 2023; energy-innovation-austria biomass article
notes: €35M investment converted power plant boiler to 100% biomass (300,000 t/yr biomass required) — ~30% CO₂ footprint reduction. Biomass conversion complete ~2022. River Mur location. Austria lacks CO₂ storage. Low retrofit score despite active sustainability investment.

name: Zellstoff Pöls (Heinzel Group) Kraft Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~430,000 t/yr pulp + ~80,000 t/yr bleached kraft paper; Pöls (Tauernstraße 15, 8761 Pöls), Styria; expansion to >500,000 t announced
operator: Zellstoff Pöls AG (Heinzel Group; Heinzel Holding Austria)
source: Heinzel Group expansion announcement; Andritz Pöls largest new paper machine (PM2 startup); Manufacturing Today Zellstoff Pöls; Heinzelpoels.com About us
notes: Styria, near Judenburg. Heinzel Group investing in major capacity expansion (>500,000 t/yr pulp). New paper machine PM2 from Andritz started up 2024 — Europe's largest new paper machine. Despite large scale, Austria's absence of CO₂ storage keeps retrofit score low. Pulp expansion increases biogenic CO₂ significantly.

name: Navigator Company Figueira da Foz Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~570,000 t/yr BEKP pulp + ~800,000 t/yr UWF paper; Figueira da Foz, Coimbra district, coast
source: Navigator Company Figueira da Foz mill page; EIB EUR 40M loan 2018 (energy efficiency); EUWID storm damage 2024; Navigator SEC filings; calc: 570 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt
notes: Coastal location on Atlantic — good for future offshore CO₂ storage via Portuguese offshore basins (Lusitanian Basin) or potential Atlantic transport. Integrated pulp+paper mill. Navigator announced decarbonization roadmap but no CCS. Portugal is developing offshore CCS framework. Medium retrofit score for coastal access.

name: Navigator Company Setúbal Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~550,000 t/yr BEKP pulp; Setúbal, Setúbal district, Sado estuary
source: Navigator Company Wikipedia; Navigator-USA corporate PDF; Navigator investors PDF; calc: 550 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt
notes: Setúbal (south of Lisbon). Industrial port area on Sado estuary. Located near the Portimão industrial corridor and Sines port (Portugal's main deep-water port and potential CO₂ export terminal). Medium retrofit score — coastal + port access gives good future CCS transport options.

name: Altri Celbi Pulp Mill (Leirosa)
capacity_note: ~800,000 t/yr BEKP pulp (world record production lines); Leirosa, Figueiró dos Vinhos municipality, coastal
source: Celbi website production capacity; Andritz Celbi world record article; Altri SGPS investor relations; calc: 800 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt
notes: Leirosa, Figueiró dos Vinhos, coastal Coimbra district. One of the most efficient global eucalyptus pulp producers (multiple Andritz world records). Atlantic coastal location. No CCS announced but Altri Group has active sustainability targets. Same coastal advantages as Navigator Figueira da Foz.

name: Ence Navia Biofactory (Pulp Mill)
capacity_note: 685,000 t/yr ECF eucalyptus pulp (post-Navia 80 expansion); Navia estuary, Asturias
source: Ence Navia Biofactory page; Andritz Ence Navia 80 expansion article; Ence AGM 2025 biogenic CO₂ statement (>4 Mt/yr total); calc: 685 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt
notes: Post-expansion to 685,000 t/yr (Navia 80 project via Andritz). Ence claims >4 Mt/yr biogenic CO₂ potential across both mills — working on CO₂ capture engineering + green hydrogen + synthetic fuels for maritime/aviation. Navia estuary location; no CO₂ storage in Spain — CCU pathway more likely than CCS.

name: Ence Pontevedra Biofactory (Pulp Mill)
capacity_note: 515,000 t/yr BEK eucalyptus pulp; Ría de Pontevedra estuary, Galicia

name: Mondi Świecie Containerboard & Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~600,000 t/yr bleached + unbleached pulp; 6 paper machines; major Kujawsko-Pomorskie industrial site
source: Mondi Świecie S.A. CEWEP/seat document; Mondi €95M investment completion 2024; Andritz major pulp capacity increase at Mondi Świecie; GEM Wiki Swiecie Mill power station

Poland developing CCS strategy; Mondi has SBTi net-zero targets. Medium retrofit score — large source, active investment, but Poland CCS infrastructure nascent.

name: Mayr-Melnhof / IP Kwidzyn Pulp & Paperboard Mill
capacity_note: ~400,000 t/yr kraft pulp + ~740,000 t/yr paperboard/UFS on 4 paper machines; Kwidzyn, Pomerania

notes: Formerly International Paper's largest European mill. Sold to Mayr-Melnhof 2021. Largest integrated pulp+paper mill in Poland by paper output. Pulp production ~400 kt/yr market + fluff. MM Karton has sustainability program but no CCS plans. Low retrofit score — ownership transition, no CCS policy framework in Poland for mills.

name: Arctic Paper Kostrzyn nad Odrą Paper & Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~315,000 t/yr uncoated woodfree paper + integrated pulp production; Kostrzyn nad Odrą, Western Poland
source: Arctic Paper Kostrzyn mill page; EUWID capacity expansion article; GEM Wiki Kostrzyn paper mill power station; paper-world.com Arctic Paper Kostrzyn
notes: Western Poland on Oder River — border with Germany. Integrated pulp-paper mill. Largest offset paper producer in Poland. No CCS. Proximity to Germany could facilitate future cross-border CO₂ transport if German CCS infrastructure expands.

name: Mondi Štětí Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~600,000 t/yr bleached/unbleached pulp + 210,000 t/yr new kraft paper (PM added 2024); Štětí, Ústecký Region, Elbe River
source: Mondi Štětí location page; GEM Wiki Mondi Steti power station; Papnews 70 years article; Mondi €470M modernisation plan; packaging-gateway new PM article; coordinates from Open Infrastructure Map (50.46091835, 14.37585352)
notes: Czech Republic's largest paper mill (70+ years history). New 210,000 t/yr kraft paper machine started 2024 (€470M modernization). Two fibre lines. Located on Elbe River — potential CO₂ transport corridor northward to North Sea storage. Mondi SBTi targets. Medium retrofit score.

name: Mondi SCP Ružomberok Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~580,000 t/yr uncoated fine paper + ~310,000 t/yr containerboard + 100,000 t/yr market pulp; Ružomberok, Žilina region
source: Mondi SCP Slovakia location page; Andritz ANDRITZ spectrum 31 Ružomberok; Mondi SBTi targets 2022; Open Infrastructure Map coordinates (49.0786326, 19.3338346); Mondi new biomass power plant 2025 announcement
notes: Slovakia's largest integrated pulp and paper mill. New biomass power plant announced 2025 (Mondi) to increase energy self-sufficiency to 90% — reduces fossil CO₂ but increases biogenic CO₂ throughput. Slovakia has no CO₂ storage infrastructure. Low retrofit score despite large biogenic source.

name: Mercer Stendal Biomass Power (co-located with pulp mill)
capacity_note: 148 MWe biomass/bioenergy CHP — power sold to grid; bark, wood residues, black liquor energy recovery
operator: Mercer International Inc. (Mercer Stendal GmbH) — power plant is co-registered with pulp operations
source: GEM Wiki Stendal Mill power station; Mercer International Stendal page (148 MWe figure); Germany biogenic CO₂ dynamics study PMC 2024
notes: Co-located with Mercer Stendal pulp mill (separate entry). The 148 MWe power plant is one of Germany's largest biomass electricity generators. Black liquor recovery boiler is dominant CO₂ source. High biogenic CO₂ concentration in flue gas. Academic BECCS studies (Springer, PMC 2024) list Stendal among Germany's top priority kraft BECCS sites.

name: UPM Augsburg Paper Mill (biomass CHP)
capacity_note: Europe's largest paper mill site; ~1,600,000 t/yr paper; CHP plant providing process energy; biomass fraction significant
source: UPM Augsburg mill page; UPM Augsburg CHP inauguration Nov 2022; UPM EMAS report 2024 Augsburg; GEM Wiki Augsburg Mill power station
notes: New state-of-the-art CHP inaugurated November 2022. Europe's largest paper mill by volume. Note: UPM Augsburg is primarily a paper mill using purchased pulp (no kraft recovery boiler) — biogenic CO₂ from biomass CHP + paper process is moderate. No CCS planned. UPM has Finnish BECCS activities but German plants not in current scope.

name: Energie AG Wien Simmering Biomass CHP
capacity_note: ~66 MWe + district heat; dedicated biomass (wood chips) CHP; Vienna-Simmering industrial zone
operator: Wien Energie GmbH (City of Vienna); Waste2Value initiative
source: Wien Smart City Waste2Value project; Siemens Energy Wien Energie waste-to-energy reference; Wien Energie CHP portfolio
notes: Vienna Simmering industrial corridor. Large biomass CHP for district heating and electricity. Part of Wien Energie's decarbonization program. Austria lacks CO₂ storage — low retrofit score. Potential long-term: CO₂ pipeline to Adriatic/North Sea via CEF infrastructure.

name: Attero Wilp Biogas & Bio-LNG Plant
capacity_note: Biogas from VFG (vegetable/fruit/garden) waste; Bio-LNG plant opened Sep 2024 (Queen Máxima inauguration); Wilp, Gelderland
operator: Attero B.V. / Nordsol (Bio-LNG plant is Nordsol technology)
source: Nordsol Wilp case study; Attero Wilp location page; Attero Bio-LNG inauguration Sep 2024
notes: VFG (biowaste) anaerobic digestion produces biogas → upgraded to biomethane → Nordsol liquefies to Bio-LNG. CO₂ stream from upgrading (~35–45% of raw biogas by volume) is near-pure biogenic stream. Currently vented or sold for food/beverage use. Netherlands CCS policy supportive — biogas upgrading CO₂ streams are identified as low-cost CCS candidates. Medium retrofit score: pure CO₂ stream, supportive policy, but small scale.

name: German Biogas Cluster — Bayern/Baden-Württemberg Agricultural AD
capacity_note: ~9,500 agricultural biogas plants in Germany (>50% in Bavaria/BW/NRW); total ~8 GW installed; aggregated CO₂ from upgrading ~2–5 Mt/yr nationally
operator: Multiple operators (municipal, agricultural cooperatives, ENGIE, EnBW, BayWa r.e., etc.)
source: German Biogas Association (Fachverband Biogas) 2024 statistics; DENA biogas atlas; IEA Bioenergy Task 37 Germany; calc: representative largest plant cluster
notes: This entry represents the aggregated opportunity from Germany's ~650 biomethane upgrading plants (out of 9,500 total biogas). Each upgrading plant emits ~1,000–10,000 t CO₂/yr as near-pure biogenic stream. Individual plants too small for standalone CCS — aggregation networks (e.g., Thüga, WINGAS pipeline clusters) needed. BMWK studying biogas-to-BECCS pathways (2024 report). Centroid approx. southern Germany high-density zone. Coordinates represent cluster centroid, not a single plant.

name: Italian Biogas Cluster — Po Valley Agricultural AD
capacity_note: ~1,600 biogas plants in Italy (~1.4 GW); >60% in Po Valley (Lombardia, Veneto, Emilia-Romagna); cattle/pig manure + energy crops
operator: Multiple (cooperatives, large farms, Agrinord, Bioenergia Fiemme, Snam/ENI biomethane offtake)
source: CIB (Consorzio Italiano Biogas) 2024 report; GSE Italy biogas statistics; IEA Bioenergy Task 37 Italy chapter
notes: Po Valley biogas cluster is second-largest in EU after Germany. Snam is developing biomethane-to-grid infrastructure. ENI's Ravenna offshore CCS hub (under development) could eventually receive biogenic CO₂ from upgraded Po Valley biogas — creating a regional BECCS value chain. Centroid approx. Cremona area. Coordinates represent cluster centroid.

name: EnviTec Biogas Güstrow Biomethane Plant
capacity_note: ~80 GWh/yr biomethane (one of Germany's largest single agricultural AD + upgrading plants); cattle slurry + silage; Güstrow, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern
operator: EnviTec Biogas AG (listed; Deutsche Biogas/Envitec subsidiary)
source: EnviTec Biogas AG annual report; German Biogas Association plant register; IEA Bioenergy Task 37 Germany country report
notes: Representative large German agricultural biomethane plant. Güstrow area has multiple EnviTec/NAWARO facilities. CO₂ from biogas upgrading is near-pure biogenic stream — currently vented or sold commercially. Germany's planned biogas strategy (2024 BMWK) is developing frameworks for CO₂ capture from upgrading plants. Small scale per site — aggregation needed for economical CCS.

name: Shanghai Laogang WtE Phase I+II
capacity_note: 6,000 t/d total (8 × 750 t/d grates); 210 MW gross
operator: Shanghai Laogang Renewable Energy Co. (MHIEC/Shanghai Environment Group)
source: MHI press release 2017; Recycling International 2019; GEM Shanghai Laogang power station
notes: World's largest WtE by throughput capacity; biogenic fraction ~50% of MSW; concentrated flue stack amenable to post-combustion capture. Weak regional CO2 storage pipeline; regulatory pathway uncertain (thesis sourcing risk flag for East Asia).

name: Shenzhen Bao'an Energy Ecological Park
capacity_note: ~9,000 t/d (5 lines × ~1,800 t/d); 135 MW (Baoan III alone); ~3 Mt/yr throughput
operator: Keppel Seghers / Shenzhen Greenland Environmental Group
source: Keppel Seghers factsheet; Power Technology Baoan III profile; GEM Guangdong Shenzhen Bao'an power station
notes: Five-line complex in Songgang, Bao'an District. Largest single WtE campus outside Laogang. Biogenic fraction ~50% MSW. Sourcing risk as for all East Asia facilities.

name: Guangzhou Likeng WtE (Phase I + II)
capacity_note: ~3,290 t/d combined (Phase I 1,040 t/d + Phase II 2,250 t/d); 40+ MW
operator: Guangzhou Environment Group / Babcock & Wilcox (Phase II technology)
source: Dong thesis (WTERT 2020); B&W case study Likeng II; IPEN case study 2015
notes: Located Baiyun District, Guangzhou. Phase I operational since 2006. Combined among the larger plants in Guangdong. Biogenic ~50%. Weak storage/regulatory context.

name: Beijing Asuwei WtE Plant
capacity_note: 3,000 t/d; ~420 GWh/yr electricity generation
source: Power Technology Beijing Asuwei profile; Beijing government waste facility data 2023; Lu Li Columbia thesis
notes: Located Xiaotangshan, Changping District, Beijing. Commissioned Sep 2019. Processes Changping and north-city waste. Biogenic ~50% of MSW. Coordinates are centroid of Xiaotangshan town; exact facility at approx 40.20°N 116.42°E based on Changping district location.

name: Hangzhou Linjiang WtE Complex
capacity_note: ~2 Mt/yr throughput across 10 incineration plants; >1 billion kWh/yr
operator: Hangzhou Linjiang Environmental Energy Co., Ltd.
source: Xinhua / China.org.cn June 2026; Dong thesis WTERT 2020
notes: Hangzhou manages a city-wide WtE network; the Jiufeng facility is the central anchor. Coordinates approximate for Hangzhou east urban/industrial zone. Biogenic ~50% of processed MSW.

name: Chengdu Wanxing WtE Plant
capacity_note: est. 2,000 t/d; 50 MW

notes: Sichuan province; capacity note and CO2 estimate are approximations—facility-level public data limited. Biogenic ~50% MSW assumed. Weak storage/regulatory context.

name: Tokyo Shin-Koto Incineration Plant
capacity_note: 1,800 t/d; 50 MW; Japan's largest single WtE facility
source: Fuji Electric case study; Clean Authority of Tokyo official site; GEM Shinkoto power station
notes: Located 3-1-1 Yumenoshima, Koto-ku, Tokyo. Biogenic fraction of Japanese MSW ~50%. Japan has no operational geological CO2 storage; retrofit would require offshore storage development.

name: Osaka Maishima WtE Facility
capacity_note: 300,000 t/yr MSW; 32 MW
source: Power Technology Maishima profile; Industry About Osaka Maishima; GEM Maishima power station
notes: Iconic architecture by Friedensreich Hundertwasser. Commissioned 2001. Smaller scale; retrofit score low due to modest size and urban location constraints.

name: Yokohama Tsurumi Incineration Plant
source: Japan MOE waste management report; Power Engineering MHI upgrade article 2024
notes: Yokohama operates multiple WtE plants; Tsurumi (Minato) cited at 900 t/d, 22 MW. MHI unit performing upgrades as of 2024. Biogenic ~50% Japanese MSW.

source: Seoul Solution Mapo Resource Recovery Facility article; Korea Times 2020
notes: Located Sangam-dong, Mapo District. Serves five central Seoul districts. Small scale; low retrofit score. One of four Seoul WtE plants.

source: Korea Times 2020; Korea Herald 2024; calc estimate based on scale comparison with Seoul plants

name: Taipei Beitou Refuse Incineration Plant
operator: Taipei City Government (Dept. of Environmental Protection)
source: Wikipedia Beitou Refuse Incineration Plant; GEM Beitou Refuse incinerator power station; Taiwan EMA data
notes: Located Zhoumei Borough, Beitou District. Taiwan operates dense network of WtE plants; Beitou is among the largest. Biogenic ~50% MSW. Taiwan has nascent CCS regulatory framework.

notes: Kaohsiung operates four WtE plants (Central, South, Renwu, Gangshan) with combined 5,400 t/d. Entry represents the Central District plant as the largest. Biogenic ~50% MSW.

notes: 26 Office Rd, East Rockingham, Kwinana Industrial Area. Australia's first operating large-scale WtE plant. 29 MW; biogenic ~40% Australian MSW. Adjacent to Kwinana Industrial Area—potential industrial CCS cluster with proximity to offshore basins.

name: Avertas Energy Kwinana WtE (formerly Kwinana EfW)
capacity_note: 400,000 t/yr; 36 MW (planned/under development)
source: Minister for Industry media release; Energy Magazine WA WtE article; CEFC case study
notes: Located Kwinana, 4.5 km from East Rockingham plant. $113M government funding committed. Biogenic ~40% Australian MSW. Development status as of 2026 not fully confirmed—listed as planned.

name: APP Indah Kiat Perawang Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~1.9 Mt/yr pulp + paper; one of the world's largest single-site pulp mills
operator: PT Indah Kiat Pulp & Paper Tbk (APP Sinar Mas)
source: Indah Kiat company website; Papermart APP profile; GEM mill records
notes: Jl. Raya Minas–Perawang Km 26, Siak Regency, Riau. Black liquor combustion in kraft recovery boilers is the primary large biogenic CO2 point source. Emissions estimate based on industry benchmarks (~1.8 tCO2/t pulp for recovery boiler + biomass boiler combined). Storage risk: Sumatra has limited proximate geological storage; thesis sourcing-risk flag applies.

name: APP Indah Kiat Serang Paper Mill
capacity_note: est. 500,000 t/yr paper; printing/writing focus
operator: PT Indah Kiat Pulp & Paper Tbk (APP Sinar Mas)
source: Indah Kiat company website; APP sustainability report 2018
notes: Jl. Raya Serang Km 76, Kragilan, Serang, Banten (West Java). Integrated paper mill. Lower kraft-pulp fraction than Perawang means lower biogenic CO2 intensity; estimate is partial (biomass boilers + some recovery boiler contribution).

name: Tjiwi Kimia Paper Mill (APP)
capacity_note: ~1.2 Mt/yr paper + board; ~320,000 t/yr stationery converting
operator: PT Pabrik Kertas Tjiwi Kimia Tbk (APP Sinar Mas)
source: Tjiwi Kimia company profile; GEM Tjiwi Kimia Paper Mill power station; Paperindex Indonesia listing
notes: Jl. Raya Surabaya–Mojokerto Km 44, Tarik, Sidoarjo, East Java. Large integrated mill; biomass and black liquor combustion. GEM lists on-site power station at 300+ MW.

name: Nine Dragons Paper Dongguan Mill
capacity_note: 5.85 Mt/yr (16 paper machines); world's largest single-site containerboard complex
source: Nine Dragons Dongguan Base page; Wikipedia Nine Dragons Paper Holdings; GEM Lee & Man Paper power station (comparable facility cross-check)
notes: Songshan Lake Hi-Tech Zone, Dongguan, Guangdong. Primarily uses recycled fibre (OCC) rather than virgin kraft pulp, so biogenic CO2 is lower intensity than kraft mills but still large in absolute terms due to biomass/gas boilers and massive steam demand. CO2 estimate is conservative. Weak storage pipeline—Guangdong offshore basins in early development.

name: Sun Paper Group Yanzhou Mill
capacity_note: 4.6 Mt/yr total group capacity; Yanzhou headquarters mill is largest site
operator: Shandong Sun Holdings Group Co., Ltd.
source: Paperindex Sun Paper profile; company website description; GEM records
notes: Yanzhou District, Jining, Shandong Province. Integrated forestry-pulp-paper; virgin kraft pulp component drives biogenic CO2 via recovery boilers. Large captive power plant burns biomass/black liquor. Shandong coal province—CO2 transport infrastructure being developed.

name: Chenming Paper Shouguang (Meilun) Mill

source: Wikipedia Chenming Paper; GEM Chenming Mill Shouguang Meilun Paper Mill captive power station (545 MW on-site); Papermart top China mills
notes: Shouguang City, Weifang, Shandong. 545 MW captive power station on-site—large concentrated CO2 source. GEM lists this as operating. Biogenic CO2 from black liquor recovery boilers and biomass combustion.

source: GEM Lee & Man Paper power station; Fisher & Co. semi-chemical pulp analysis; chinapulppaper.com
notes: He Xi Industrial Park, Hongmei Town, Dongguan, Guangdong. GEM lists ≥216 MW on-site power station. Primarily recycled fibre; biogenic CO2 from biomass boilers and waste heat recovery. Estimate conservative.

name: Nippon Paper Ishinomaki Mill
capacity_note: 643,000 t/yr woodpulp; 370,000 t/yr DIP; ~1.1 Mt/yr paper
source: Andritz Nippon Paper spectrum article; Nippon Paper Group domestic mills page; GEM Ishinomaki Mill power station
notes: Ishinomaki City, Miyagi Prefecture. Large kraft pulp mill with integrated recovery boilers — concentrated biogenic CO2. Japan government has CCS roadmap targeting offshore geological storage.

name: Oji Paper Tomakomai Mill
capacity_note: >1 Mt/yr paper (11 machines); world's largest newsprint mill
source: Oji Paper Andritz profile; Wikimapia Oji Paper Tomakomai Mill; GEM Tomakomai power station
notes: Oji-machi 2-chome, Tomakomai, Hokkaido. Operational since 1910; now world's largest newsprint mill. Large recovery boilers and biomass power plant on-site. Tomakomai has Japan's only operating CCS pilot (METI/JCCS) — high retrofit strategic value.

name: Nippon Paper Yatsushiro Mill
capacity_note: est. 400,000–600,000 t/yr pulp and paper
source: Nippon Paper Group domestic mills page; Andritz Nippon Paper spectrum
notes: Yatsushiro City, Kumamoto Prefecture, Kyushu. One of Nippon Paper's integrated kraft mills. Capacity estimate approximate — Nippon Paper does not publish per-mill capacity publicly.

name: Daio Paper Mishima Mill
capacity_note: ~2.1 Mt/yr paper + board; ~8% of Japan's total production
source: Daio Paper key locations page; GEM Daio Mishima Mill power station; JSTAGE Mishima Mill article
notes: Coastal Seto Inland Sea location, Ehime Prefecture. 1.6 million m² site. In-house kraft pulp production with recovery boilers. Daio has stated plans for biomass/waste power co-firing. Concentrated CO2 at recovery boiler stack — high retrofit score.

name: ITC Bhadrachalam Paperboards & Specialty Papers
capacity_note: 1,400 t/d pulp (~511,000 t/yr); India's largest wood-based paper mill
operator: ITC Limited — Paperboards & Specialty Papers Division
source: Pulp and Paper Times article — capacity upgrade to 1,400 t/d; ITC PSPD website; Wikimapia ITC PSPD BCM; latitude.to coordinates confirmed
notes: Sarapaka village, Bhadradri Kothagudem district, Telangana. India's largest wood-based paper plant. Kraft recovery boilers are primary biogenic CO2 source. India has nascent CCS regulatory framework; Deccan Traps basalt and Gondwana coal seams as potential storage. Medium retrofit score reflecting policy uncertainty.

name: JK Paper Mills Rayagada (JKPM)

source: JK Paper company website; Indiamart JKPM profile; Rayagada coordinates from latlong.net; capacity from scribd JK Paper report
notes: Jaykaypur, Rayagada District, Odisha. Kraft process with recovery boilers. JK Paper recently invested ~Rs 1,775 crore in expansion. Biogenic CO2 from recovery boiler black liquor combustion.

name: Tamil Nadu Newsprint & Papers Ltd (TNPL) Kagithapuram
capacity_note: est. 400,000 t/yr paper; bagasse-based pulp
operator: Tamil Nadu Newsprint and Papers Limited (Government of Tamil Nadu)
source: Wikipedia TNPL; latitude.to TNPL coordinates (11.0488°N, 77.9977°E); TNPL company website
notes: Kagithapuram, Karur District, Tamil Nadu. World's largest bagasse-based pulp mill — biogenic CO2 from bagasse combustion in recovery/biomass boilers. Cauvery River dependency noted. State government operator.

name: West Coast Paper Mills Dandeli
capacity_note: est. 200,000+ t/yr paper; 240 acres integrated mill
source: Westcoast Paper website; Paperindex WCPM profile; Mappls coordinates for Dandeli mill at ~15.25°N 74.62°E
notes: Bangur Nagar, Dandeli, Uttara Kannada, Karnataka. Established 1955; wood-based integrated kraft mill. Remote location; low retrofit score due to infrastructure constraints and lack of proximate CO2 storage.

name: Opal Australian Paper Maryvale Mill
capacity_note: 550,000 t/yr paper (5 machines); 3 pulp mills on-site
operator: Opal Australian Paper (Nippon Paper Industries majority owner)
source: Wikipedia Australian Paper; Opal company website; Latrobe Council buffer report; Maryvale EfW infrastructure pipeline
notes: Maryvale, Latrobe Valley, Victoria — operating since 1937. Australia's largest and only remaining integrated kraft pulp+paper mill. Recovery boilers and biomass boilers are large concentrated biogenic CO2 sources. Maryvale EfW facility (Veolia) also co-located. Gippsland has potential offshore storage in Bass Strait; high retrofit score.

name: Visy Tumut Kraft Mill

source: Visy Tumut Kraft Mill page; Tumut mill environmental approvals; Waze maps address 436 Gadara Rd Tumut confirmed town location
notes: Gadara Road, Tumut, NSW. Pine plantation-based kraft mill. Uses radiata pine from Softwood forests. Recovery boilers are primary biogenic CO2 point source. Potential storage in Gunnedah Basin or offshore Otway. High retrofit score: single-site large source, private operator with sustainability commitments.

name: Oji Fibre Solutions Kinleith Mill

operator: Oji Fibre Solutions (NZ) Ltd. (Oji Holdings, Japan)
source: Wikipedia Kinleith Mill; WorkSafe NZ major hazard facility public info; Engineering NZ heritage record; coordinates -38.2745, 175.8855 from heritage records
notes: Kinleith, 7 km south of Tokoroa, South Waikato. Kraft recovery boilers are principal biogenic CO2 source. New Zealand has Taranaki offshore storage potential and government CCS policy emerging. Paper production cessation (2025) reduces overall throughput but pulp line continues.

source: Industry About Pan Pac Whirinaki; Pan Pac company website; Wikipedia Pan Pac Forest Products; coordinates -39.381035, 176.888235 confirmed
notes: 1161 SH2 Wairoa Road, Whirinaki, 20 km north of Napier, Hawke's Bay. BCTMP (bleached chemi-thermomechanical pulp) process — lower biogenic CO2 than kraft but still significant biomass combustion for steam. Bark and wood waste boilers are CO2 source.

Vietnam has no operational CO2 storage; regulatory framework absent — thesis sourcing risk flag applies strongly.

notes: Kanda-machi, Miyako-gun, Fukuoka Prefecture, Kyushu. 100% wood biomass (imported woodchips + domestic). Concentrated single-stack ~0.41 Mt CO2/yr. Japan's FIT regime supports biomass; CCS retrofit would benefit from METI CCUS roadmap. Coordinates approximate for Kanda-machi.

notes: Port of Omaezaki, Omaezaki City, Shizuoka Prefecture; 53,000 m² harbourside site. New plant (2025). Concentrated biogenic CO2 from dedicated biomass combustion. High retrofit score: new infrastructure, utility-grade operator.

capacity_note: ~5.5 Mt cane/yr (Ipaussu unit, one of Tereos Brazil's 7 plants); São Paulo state
operator: Tereos Group (French cooperative; 7 Brazil mills total)
source: Tereos Group Brazil operations; Hydrocarbon Processing 'Brazil mills boost sugar capacity' Mar 2024; calc: ~81 kg CO2/t cane × 5.5 Mt = 0.45 Mt CO2
notes: Ipaussu, São Paulo state. Tereos is France's largest sugar group, with 7 plants in Brazil (~30 Mt/yr combined crushing across portfolio). Prioritizes sugar over ethanol in 2024 flex. Fermentation CO2 is pure stream. European Tereos parent has some CCS awareness but no Brazil CCS plans. Moderate retrofit score for São Paulo location near industry.

name: Ledesma Ingenio Sugar/Ethanol Mill

source: Wikipedia Ledesma S.A.A.I.; Sugaronline ethanol expansion 2017; Encyclopedia.com Ledesma company history; Wikimapia Ingenio Ledesma coords (23°49'38"S, 64°47'20"W = -23.83, -64.79)
notes: Libertador General San Martín, Jujuy province (Andean foothills, NW Argentina). Diversified operations: sugarcane, sugar, ethanol, paper, cellulose. 51 MW bagasse cogeneration. Argentina has no CCS infrastructure and limited storage geology in Jujuy region. Ledesma also operates forestry/paper division. Low retrofit score: governance/regulatory context, lack of infrastructure.

source: GEM Wiki Ingenio Tabacal power station; Seaboard Corp Tabacal company page; location: Hipólito Yrigoyen, ~25 km from Orán, Salta
notes: Hipólito Yrigoyen (El Tabacal), Salta, Argentina (~23.2°S, 64.3°W est. from proximity to Orán). Sugar, ethanol, and 30 MW cogeneration from bagasse. Seaboard Corp US-owned. Remote Andean foothills location. No CCS. Lower priority than Ledesma due to smaller scale.

name: Incauca Sugar Mill & Bioethanol Plant
capacity_note: 70 MW cogeneration (33 MWh avg, 10 MWh to grid); sugarcane bioethanol; El Ortigal, Cauca dept.
operator: Ingenio del Cauca S.A.S. (Incauca; Cauca Valley sugar group)
source: Incauca location page (El Ortigal, 50 km from Cali, 134 km from Popayán); Incauca history page; Sugar mills in Colombia overview; WEG solutions Colombia article
notes: El Ortigal, Cauca Department, Colombia (50 km from Cali). Colombia's largest sugar mill. 70 MW cogeneration from bagasse. Sugarcane ethanol (not corn — not excluded by Frontier). Fermentation CO2 is pure stream. Colombia has no CO2 storage infrastructure and limited CCS policy. Low retrofit score but notable as largest Colombian sugar facility.

name: Manuelita Sugar & Bioethanol Mill
capacity_note: ~4.2 Mt cane/yr; integrated sugar, ethanol, biofuels; Palmira, Valle del Cauca

notes: Felixton, Empangeni area, KZN north coast (~160 km north of Durban). Part of Tongaat Hulett's three KZN mills (Felixton, Maidstone, Amatikulu). capacity_note: ~100 MWth biomass CHP district heating (wood residues, bark); Cherepovets, Vologda Oblast

Severstal's forestry operations generate substantial wood residues. Many small-medium biomass CHP plants operate in this region for district heating. No CCS policy in Russia's biomass energy sector. name: URE Barueri Waste-to-Energy Plant (Orizon)
capacity_note: ~20 MW; 825 t/day (~300 kt/yr MSW); first Latin American mass-burn WtE; Barueri, São Paulo metro
operator: Orizon Valorização de Resíduos S.A. (SENER engineering)

notes: Barueri, São Paulo metropolitan area (~26.5 km from São Paulo center). First mass-burn WtE plant in Latin America under construction (designed by SENER for Orizon). Operations expected ~2027. 300 kt/yr MSW throughput, 20 MW. Brazil MSW is biogenic-rich (~60%). Biogenic CO2 est: ~0.08 Mt/yr (50% of total ~0.16 Mt). Too small for commercial CCS. Important as Brazil's inaugural WtE BECCS candidate.

name: Arauco Sucuruí Pulp Mill, Mato Grosso do Sul (planned)
